verdict.rationale: Unreal has extensive first-party API documentation: C++ gameplay programming, a generated per-class Unreal Python API reference served to non-browser clients, Python autocomplete stubs, and Remote Control HTTP/WebSocket references. Epic also serves llms.txt, though intermittently. But nothing shows LLM-generated code works on the first try. API stability is undercut by the Python API's Experimental label and a community report that new engine versions break things. Public examples are limited because engine source is EULA/account-gated and returns 'Not Found' to unauthenticated GitHub API requests. Missing for 10: any evidence of LLM first-try code success, evidence of stable APIs across versions, abundant publicly crawlable examples or source, and reliable agent access to docs (WAF 403s, no markdown docs).
